scientific_interpretation: Groq and OpenRouter both produced five valid, semantically stable, protected-correct environment/tooling classifications. Together with EXP-L Pilot 5, this supplies a second two-provider stable-correct control while again showing a large provider latency gap. Stability remains non-authoritative because Pilots 2 and 4 already demonstrate zero-entropy stable-wrong cases.
design_consequences: Retain stable-correct controls across more than one defect class.
Evaluate review triggering against protected correctness, not entropy alone.
Use measured latency and token cost in EXP-K alongside correctness.
Do not generalize OpenRouter latency from a small free-tier sample, but retain it as observed routing evidence.
limitations: The bundle used semantic proxy version 1.1 before mixed-cause signatures were added; this case has a single defect class so that limitation does not affect its class-level result.
Only one case per defect class is represented here.
